You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which statement is a normative statement?

options.A: China has never had a balance of payments surplus.
options.B: Higher interest rates might reduce investment.
options.C: Perfect competition is allocatively efficient.
options.D: Welfare payments should be increased.

questions.questionText: What do economists regard as the reward for taking risks and organising production?

options.B: interest
options.C: wages
options.D: profit

questions.questionText: The British pound is the national currency of the UK. In Brixton in south London it is possible to get a distinctively marked currency called the Brixton pound from special cash machines. This can be spent with 150 local shopkeepers. Similar schemes are found in towns in the US, Italy and France. Should Brixton pounds be considered money?

options.A: no, because it is not possible to have two currencies in a country
options.B: no, because they are not generally acceptable outside of Brixton
options.C: yes, because some shopkeepers are willing to accept them
options.D: yes, because they fulfil all the functions of money

questions.questionText: When stating the law of demand for a good, economists use the phrase ‘all other things being equal’. What is not one of these ‘all other things’?

options.B: the price of other goods
options.C: the price of the good
options.D: the tastes of the consumer

questions.questionText: What will not cause a shift in the market supply curve of a commodity?

options.B: a rise in the price of a factor input
options.C: a rise in the price of the commodity
options.D: the introduction of a specific tax on the commodity

questions.questionText: A product has a low price elasticity of supply. What might explain this?

options.A: The product has a low opportunity cost.
options.B: The product is highly perishable.
options.C: The product is classed as an inferior good.
options.D: The product is considered to be a necessity.

questions.questionText: A car manufacturer estimates that the price elasticity of supply of its cars is +2.5. What will be the impact of a 10% increase in price?

options.B: a 25% rise in total revenue
options.C: a 2.5% fall in quantity supplied
options.D: a 25% rise in quantity supplied

A UK based food company wishes to diversify its product range. To finance this, it has obtained a $10m loan from a bank to buy land, build and equip a bakery. What would not be classified by an economist as a factor of production?

options.A: the $10m loan used to finance the project
options.B: the land on which the bakery will be built
options.C: the ovens required to bake the bread
options.D: the soya used in the making of the bread

questions.questionText: A country’s central bank has commissioned a report on the demand for and price of houses. What might be the most likely combination of reasons for an increase in the price and quantity demanded of houses? wages of incomes interest rates bricklayers

options.B: down up unchanged
options.C: unchanged up down
options.D: up down unchanged

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the outcome when a landowner, who had allowed motorists to park on his field at no cost, introduces a parking charge of $1. supply charge X $1 Y Z demand parking spaces What happens as a result of the change?

options.A: The landowner gains a surplus of Y + Z.
options.B: The motorist gains a surplus of X + Y.
options.C: The ownership of surplus Y changes.
options.D: There is a total surplus of X + Y + Z.

questions.questionText: The table gives information about the market for two models of car. number of cars sold cross elasticity of demand with model per week respect to the price of petrol 1200 cc 10000 –0.25 2000 cc 5000 –0.50 If the prices of the cars remain unchanged, but the price of petrol increases by 100%, what will be the effect on the number of cars sold per week?

options.B: no change
options.C: decrease by 5000
options.D: decrease by 15000

questions.questionText: In many countries there are goods that must be provided directly by the government. What would be the most convincing argument for such provision?

options.A: The consumption of these products may be beneficial.
options.B: The production of these products may be harmful.
options.C: The production of these products have high opportunity costs.
options.D: These products are non-rival in consumption and non-excludable.

questions.questionText: The provision of rail services is switched from the private sector to the public sector. What is necessarily correct?

options.A: The average fare charged for the service will fall.
options.B: The profitability of the service will fall.
options.C: The rail service’s management will be responsible to different owners.
options.D: There will be an increase in the number of workers employed.

A government decides to build additional public sector housing to be rented to people receiving low incomes. What is most likely to fall as a result of this increase in public sector housing?

options.B: land prices in towns and cities
options.C: rents of houses in the private sector
options.D: total government spending

questions.questionText: Government spending for a year includes these items. $m pensions for elderly people 200 welfare payments to sick people 200 spending on hospitals 150 payment to unemployed workers 100 defence spending 100 teachers’ salaries 50 What is the total of transfer payments by this government in $m?
What would be certain to cause a fall in a country’s cost of living?

options.B: a fall in the inflation rate
options.C: a negative inflation rate
options.D: a reduction in direct tax rates

questions.questionText: What is not an aim of protectionism?

options.B: to increase price of exports
options.C: to protect infant industries
options.D: to reduce the volume of imports

questions.questionText: A country with a fixed exchange rate experiences a higher rate of inflation than its trading partners. What is the likely effect on the country’s volume of exports and imports? exports imports

options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: A sudden rise in the price of imported oil caused the annual rate of inflation in a given period to be higher than expected. What might be a likely result of this?

options.B: Real wages would rise.
options.C: The balance of trade would improve.
options.D: Unemployment would fall.

questions.questionText: What may increase the benefits a country gains from international trade?

options.A: a reduction in transportation costs because of a fall in world oil prices
options.B: domestic wage rates increase at a faster rate than output per worker
options.C: the domestic labour force becomes more occupationally immobile
options.D: trading partners increase tariffs on imported goods

questions.questionText: The world trade price of cars in country Y is US$10000. At this price domestic car producers supply 100000 cars to the market and domestic consumers purchase 200000 cars. The government of country Y imposes a 10% tariff on imported cars. Under which conditions will this tariff raise the most revenue for the government? price elasticity price elasticity of of supply of car demand for cars producers in in country Y country Y
A country has a balance of trade deficit. When will this be least likely to be improved as a result of a depreciation of its currency?

options.A: if it is currently operating with a significant amount of unused resources
options.B: if the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports is less than 1
options.C: if in the long term, the price elasticity of demand for exports should increase
options.D: if the country uses a relatively small proportion of imports in their production process

questions.questionText: Which statement about trade protection is correct?

options.A: A tariff results in a greater decrease in demand for an import the lower is its price elasticity of demand.
options.B: Embargoes are only an effective trade barrier when the demand for imports is price-elastic.
options.C: Export subsidies to domestic firms will prevent the dumping of foreign products in the domestic market.
options.D: Quotas are less effective than tariffs for raising government revenue.

questions.questionText: Which type of policy would have the most immediate effect in dealing with a deflationary economic downturn?

options.B: increasing borrowing by assisting banks to lend more
options.C: investing in long-term projects to improve transport networks
options.D: switching the burden of taxation from earning to spending

questions.questionText: Which combination identifies a main aim of supply-side policy and a measure used to achieve this target? main aim policy measure

options.B: full employment increasing the money supply
options.C: income equality more progressive taxation
options.D: stable prices decreasing interest rates

questions.questionText: Deflation is associated with persistent falling price levels. Which government policy would be most effective to prevent deflation?

options.A: imposing maximum price levels on basic foodstuffs
options.B: improving consumer confidence by reducing sales taxes
options.C: increasing income tax rates and increasing government borrowing
options.D: removing economic uncertainty and encouraging business investment
